original_obligation.quoted_target: For every natural degree, derive Legendre orthogonality directly from Rodrigues, preserving actual interval integration; do not use the existing Fin 7 theorem as a universal theorem.
explicit_assumptions: The actual Mathlib shifted Legendre polynomial is Polynomial.shiftedLegendre : Nat -> Polynomial Int.
The working interval is [0,1], obtained from the original [-1,1] coordinate only by a separately proved affine change of variables.
The test polynomial p has natDegree p < n.

dirty_file_hashes.note: Existing user-dirty state is preserved and not an author input.

scope.conclusion: One universal Rodrigues orthogonality theorem over [0,1], with no finite degree cutoff.
not_claimed: The original [-1,1] Thomson kernel moment formula.
BE integrability, collision closure, historical four-axis adjudication, or scientific admission.

theorem_signature: namespace CAS12Rodrigues; noncomputable def shifted (n : Nat) : Polynomial Real := (Polynomial.shiftedLegendre n).map (Int.castRingHom Real); theorem shifted_orthogonal_lower_degree (n : Nat) (p : Polynomial Real) (hp : p.natDegree < n) : (MeasureTheory.integral (MeasureTheory.Measure.restrict MeasureTheory.volume (Set.Icc 0 1)) (fun x : Real => p.eval x * (shifted n).eval x)) = 0; end CAS12Rodrigues

commands.purpose: Compile the exact owned source against pinned Lean/mathlib.
Print theorem type and axioms after the theorem compiles.

tool_roles.wolfram_xact: NOT_NEEDED for this narrow Lean Rodrigues lemma; no tensor or curvature statement.
tool_roles.sympy: NOT_NEEDED for a universal interval-integral proof; later affine kernel specialization may use it.
tool_roles.sage_singular: NOT_NEEDED for this analytic polynomial/integration-by-parts lemma.
tool_roles.lean: Owns endpoint multiplicity, repeated integration by parts, degree derivative vanishing, and the universal interval result.

acceptance: Do not add axioms, sorry, admit, or assume the target orthogonality theorem.
Retain the first raw compile failure and each final stdout/stderr/exit record.
The final printed theorem must retain n : Nat and hp : p.natDegree < n.
Only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound are permitted in the final axiom audit.
If this exact statement cannot be made to compile due to a verified Mathlib interface mismatch, return the exact mismatch without changing the source theorem.
